mappings.note: Write a piece on India's freedom struggle, the setting in which the poem was composed: C-1.1-LO-40 for the rachna-prishthbhoomi, C-2.2 for the writing.

Imagine the letter the mother would write. C-1.1-LO-42 for her portrayal, which the letter must be built from, and C-2.2-LO-11 for the letter itself -- noting LO-11 is worded for a letter sent HOME, and this one runs the other way.
Turn the parents' conversation about the poet into written dialogue. Creative composition, C-2.2 at competency level: LO-11 is a letter and LO-12 a piece on longing, so neither form fits.
Which natural thing you would send a message by, and why -- a reasoned personal choice, C-2.1.
Where and why he wrote the poem -- from jail, for his family. The rachna-prishthbhoomi, C-1.1-LO-40.
What the unceasing rain stands for in his mind -- the rain imagery and its chosen words, C-3.2-LO-5.
The image of the mother the poem builds -- C-1.1-LO-42.
What 'vajra-bhuj navneet-sa ur' makes of the father -- C-1.1-LO-41.
What 'let one leaf fall and the flood breaks' points to -- the father's tenderness, C-1.1-LO-41.
What 'paritap' signals -- word sense, the shabd-sampada half of C-4.3-LO-25.

'And tell them I am in fine spirits' -- he is hiding his suffering from his people. No LO here covers the poet's own state (they cover the poet's life, the father and the mother), so C-1.1 at competency level.
What the poem chiefly sets out -- the ache of home and of being alone. The central idea, C-1.1 at competency level.
The many sides of the father's personality -- C-1.1-LO-41.
How he shows patience, courage and sacrifice in hardship -- the poet's own bearing, which no LO here states; C-1.1 at competency level.
How the repeated rain carries his feeling -- C-3.2-LO-5.
Record or read aloud the sound-words jhara-jhar, thar-thar, sar-sar and say what they build. C-4.3-LO-24 is the dhwanyatmakta-and-recitation outcome.
The word 'ghar' across Eighth Schedule languages -- Indian linguistic diversity, C-4.3 at competency level and CG-4; the chapter's C-4.3 LOs are sound-beauty and alankar, so neither applies.
Find another poem or story about missing home and present it: C-4.2 for engaging with Indian literary works, C-2.1 for the presentation.
Explain the regional words chhin, jhaila, tarla and bad ka jhaad and use them in new sentences -- the lokbhasha outcome C-3.2-LO-6.

Give the grammatical class of each word in the quoted lines. A pad-parichay drill, so the practical-grammar goal CG-3; no competency here covers parsing. NOTE: the options printed against it are poem lines, not answers to this task.
Draw your own family tree and write a few lines on each member -- composition, C-2.2 at competency level.
Pick the lines showing the mother's emotional strength and explain them -- C-1.1-LO-42.
Which part of the poem moves you most and why -- a reasoned personal judgement, C-2.1.
Find lines for each listed feature: C-4.3-LO-24 for the sound-beauty the item opens with, C-3.2-LO-6 for the lokbhasha row, C-4.3-LO-25 for the alankar row.
Find other works that make a natural thing the messenger -- engaging with the wider literary tradition, C-4.2.
Who wrote the poem -- poet introduction, C-1.1-LO-40.
Which state he was born in -- poet introduction, C-1.1-LO-40.
The year of his birth -- poet introduction, C-1.1-LO-40.
Which work won him the Sahitya Akademi award -- poet introduction, C-1.1-LO-40.
Which magazine he edited -- poet introduction, C-1.1-LO-40.
During which movement the poem was written -- the rachna-prishthbhoomi, C-1.1-LO-40.
How long he was imprisoned -- the background to the poem, C-1.1-LO-40.
The poem's central feeling -- the memory of family. The main idea, C-1.1 at competency level.
Which season opens the poem -- the rain-and-nature description, C-3.2-LO-5.
The mother's feeling in 'he who draws back would shame my womb' -- C-1.1-LO-42.
Why the rains reminded the father of him -- the father's view of his son, C-1.1-LO-41.
Which habit of the father is described -- sowing gourd seed in the big yard. C-1.1-LO-41.
Why the mother is likened to a cloud -- full of grief and unable to weep. C-1.1-LO-42.
For whom 'they cannot even weep for shame' is said -- the brothers and sisters, whom no LO here covers; C-1.1 at competency level.
The sense of 'nihayat nam' -- word sense, C-4.3-LO-25.
Assertion-reason on clouds likened to the mother smoothing the courtyard: C-4.3-LO-25 for the figure, C-1.1-LO-42 for the mother it draws.
The meaning of 'ur' -- word sense, C-4.3-LO-25.
Why the memory of his father's dress distresses him -- C-1.1-LO-41.
For whom 'a body like a hill, a mind like a banyan' is said -- the father, C-1.1-LO-41.
What the falling-leaf line tells of the father -- C-1.1-LO-41.
What he asks of the monsoon cloud -- rain, but do not tell them my sorrows. The poet's concealment, C-1.1 at competency level.
How he addresses the Sawan -- 'he sajeele hare sawan'. The word-choice in the rain and nature passage, C-3.2-LO-5.
What he tells the cloud to report -- that he is well and busy. C-1.1 at competency level.
Fill in 'ghar nahin hoon bas yahi hai' -- word choice, C-4.3-LO-25.
The meaning of 'viras' -- word sense, C-4.3-LO-25.
Assertion-reason on reporting that he weighs seventy ser so they are not distressed -- C-1.1 at competency level.
What he asks the cloud NOT to say -- that he wakes, shuns company and is silent. C-1.1 at competency level.
Fill in 'kaatne mein vyast hoon main' -- word choice, C-4.3-LO-25.
What 'kaanpte hain praan thar-thar' conveys -- the sound-word carrying unrest, C-4.3-LO-24.
Of whom 'thunder in his speech, a gale in his work' is said -- the father, C-1.1-LO-41.
Assertion-reason on the mother being unlettered -- C-1.1-LO-42.
Statements about the household -- four brothers, the poet the fifth child. Content recall no LO here states; C-1.1.
The meaning of 'paritap' -- word sense, C-4.3-LO-25.
Which statement about the poem is right -- a jailed poet's family memories. The main idea, C-1.1.
Which poetic feature the jhara-jhar lines carry -- anupras and sound-play, C-4.3-LO-24.
The mother's message behind 'he who draws back would shame my womb' -- C-1.1-LO-42.
Which facts of prison he asks the clouds to hide -- C-1.1 at competency level.
What he spares his people by refusing to say he is 'ast' -- C-1.1 at competency level.
Bhavaniprasad Mishra's literary and administrative life -- poet introduction, C-1.1-LO-40.
Why his heart and mind are restless -- the rain and its pull on him, C-3.2-LO-5.
The sense of 'home, that fullness of joy, that is far from me' -- the poem's central feeling, C-1.1.
How far the mother's love reaches and how he misses it -- C-1.1-LO-42.
The father's bodily and mental vigour from 'whom old age never touched' -- C-1.1-LO-41.
In what words the father's valour and fearlessness are exalted -- C-1.1-LO-41.
The father's daily round and his exercise -- C-1.1-LO-41.
What the mother said, wiping the father's tears, to steady him -- C-1.1-LO-42.
Why he calls himself luckless in 'the memory of the fifth' -- the poet's own state, C-1.1 at competency level.
Review his proud, unyielding temper from 'I shove grief aside' -- C-1.1 at competency level.
The joint family as a model of affection and strong ties -- a cultural value the poem carries, C-4.2.
A full review of the father's many-sided character -- C-1.1-LO-41.
The mother's emotional strength and vatsalya amid his imprisonment -- C-1.1-LO-42.
The meaning of 'tir raha hai' -- word sense, C-4.3-LO-25.
The meaning of 'poor' -- word sense, C-4.3-LO-25.
How many brothers he had. Content recall no LO states; C-1.1.
What the poem says of the mother -- she was unlettered. C-1.1-LO-42.
The image of the mother in 'lay my head in her lap and grief is gone' -- C-1.1-LO-42.
The sense of 'vajra-bhuj navneet-sa ur' -- arms of thunderbolt, heart of butter. C-1.1-LO-41.
What 'old age never touched him' means -- C-1.1-LO-41.
What the father's routine included -- Gita reading, dand and mugdar. C-1.1-LO-41.
Fill in 'nahin vyapa' -- word choice, C-4.3-LO-25.
Who the fifth is -- the poet himself. Content recall; C-1.1.
Of whom 'gold made finer by borax, his father kept saying' is said -- the father's regard for him, C-1.1-LO-41.
What the mother would have said of her tears -- C-1.1-LO-42.
